questions.text: If discretionary spending rises sharply, the likely outcome is:
options: Reduced surplus and possible debt increase
questions.explanation: Overspending reduces savings and may require borrowing.

questions.text: A 25-year-old with no dependants and stable income is generally more suitable for which allocation?
options: Very high proportion of assets in cash only
Higher allocation to growth assets such as equity
questions.explanation: With long time horizon and low dependants, growth assets like equity can form a higher proportion of the portfolio.

questions.text: A 'risk-averse' investor will:
options: Always choose the highest return regardless of risk
Prefer investments with lower risk for a given return
Ignore the level of risk while investing
questions.explanation: Risk-averse investors prefer lower risk for a given return and demand a risk premium for taking additional risk.

questions.text: Flat-rate interest means:
options: Interest charged only on reducing principal
Interest calculated on full principal throughout the term
questions.explanation: Flat-rate computes interest on entire loan amount for full tenure, overstating true cost.

questions.text: Regulatory constraints are most likely to apply when:
options: The investor wants to invest abroad under LRS limits
The investor invests only in mutual funds
questions.explanation: Under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 overseas annually—this acts as a regulatory constraint.

questions.text: Debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is computed as:
options: Monthly debt obligations ÷ Gross monthly income
questions.explanation: DTI assesses ability to service debt from monthly income.

questions.text: Structured products are best described as:
options: Plain-vanilla equity shares of a company
Pre-packaged investment products combining different instruments to provide a specific payoff profile
questions.explanation: Structured products usually combine underlying assets and derivatives to deliver a targeted payoff, such as capital protection plus limited upside.

questions.text: The equity cash segment refers to:
options: Buying and selling of shares for delivery or intraday in the spot market
questions.explanation: Equity cash segment deals with spot trades where securities are bought/sold for immediate delivery or intraday square-off.

questions.text: SEBI mandates that investor complaints and their resolution status must be:
options: Displayed on AMC and intermediary websites
Submitted only to the Ministry of Finance
questions.explanation: Transparency requires intermediaries to disclose complaint numbers and status on their websites.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, investor grievances should be resolved by intermediaries within:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that intermediaries resolve investor complaints within 30 days from receipt.

questions.text: Which step should come first in preparing a household budget?
options: Listing all income sources and amounts
questions.explanation: Budgeting starts with understanding total inflows before planning outflows.

questions.text: If annual income is ₹10 lakh and annual savings ₹1.5 lakh, savings ratio is:
If monthly EMIs total ₹25,000 and gross income ₹1,00,000, DTI ratio is:
To accumulate ₹10 lakh in 15 years at 9% p.a., the annual deposit required is approximately:
questions.explanation: Using FV of annuity formula, deposit ≈ 36,000 per year.

questions.text: Transmission of mutual fund units occurs when:
options: Investor wants to transfer to a friend
Investor dies and legal heir claims ownership
questions.explanation: Transmission refers to the transfer of ownership of mutual fund units to legal heirs or nominees upon death of the holder.

questions.text: A person’s income and expenses both rise 10%. The savings amount:
questions.explanation: If both rise equally in % terms, the rupee surplus remains same proportion.

questions.text: Equity investing is MOST appropriate for which type of goal?
options: Long-term goals like retirement or children’s education after 10–15 years
questions.explanation: Equity is suitable for long-term goals where short-term volatility can be tolerated.

questions.text: In a demat account, mutual fund units are held in:
questions.explanation: Demat units are stored electronically under unique ISIN codes in investor’s depository account.

questions.text: Which loan normally carries floating interest rate linked to external benchmark?
questions.explanation: Most home loans today are linked to RBI’s repo or MCLR rate.

questions.text: The expiration day for equity derivatives in India is generally:
options: Last Thursday of the expiry month
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives on NSE and BSE typically expire on the last Thursday of the contract month.

questions.text: If a borrower prepays part of the principal early in a reducing-balance loan, future interest cost:
questions.explanation: Prepayment lowers outstanding principal, thereby reducing future interest.

questions.text: Interval funds are:
options: Closed-end schemes that become open-ended during specified transaction periods
Schemes that can be bought only once a year
questions.explanation: Interval funds are a variant of closed-end funds that open for purchase and redemption at specified intervals for at least two days.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: AIFs must issue to investors:
options: A Key Information Memorandum similar to mutual funds
questions.explanation: AIFs raise funds through private placement by issuing a detailed Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) to investors.

questions.text: Bonus shares are issued to:
options: New investors in the secondary market
questions.explanation: Bonus shares are additional shares issued to existing shareholders from free reserves.

questions.text: From an advisory perspective, why is understanding different asset classes important?
options: To match assets with client’s goals, risk profile and time horizon
To help the client avoid diversification
To recommend only one product to all clients
questions.explanation: Advisers must understand asset characteristics to recommend suitable portfolios aligned to each client’s goals and risk tolerance.

questions.text: Which of the following investors typically dominate the institutional segment?
options: Mutual funds, insurance companies, pension funds and FPIs
questions.explanation: Institutional segment comprises entities like mutual funds, insurers, pension funds and foreign portfolio investors.

questions.text: Category III AIFs are characterised by:
options: Use of diverse or complex trading strategies including leverage
questions.explanation: Category III AIFs, such as hedge funds, employ complex or leverage-based trading strategies and invest in listed or unlisted securities.

questions.text: Ethics in investment advisory primarily relates to:
options: Moral principles that guide behaviour towards clients and markets
questions.explanation: Ethics refers to moral principles and standards that guide behaviour and decision-making, especially when dealing with client money and trust.

questions.text: Portfolio rebalancing frequency should balance between:
options: Market volatility and interest rate movement
Cost of rebalancing and cost of deviation from target
questions.explanation: The decision on rebalancing frequency depends on weighing the cost of rebalancing against the risk of being off-target.

questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST fundamental ethical duty of an Investment Adviser?
options: Acting in the best interest of the client (fiduciary duty)
questions.explanation: An IA has a fiduciary duty to always act in the best interest of the client, ahead of their own interest.

questions.text: Which channel most directly involves the Registered Investment Adviser (RIA) in the investment decision?
options: Client buying direct equity on their own without advice
Client investing in a mutual fund through a distributor only
Client taking model portfolio advice from an RIA and investing accordingly
Client keeping all money in a savings bank account
questions.explanation: Here, the RIA provides customised advice or model portfolios that the client implements, reflecting the advisory role specified by SEBI’s IA regulations.

questions.text: The formula to calculate EMI is:
questions.explanation: EMI = P r (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n − 1), where P=principal, r=periodic rate, n=number of periods.

questions.text: The coefficient of correlation between portfolio and market returns is denoted by:
questions.explanation: ρ (rho) represents the correlation coefficient between two variables—in this case, portfolio and market returns.

questions.text: The seller (writer) of a call option has:
options: The right to buy the asset
The obligation to sell the asset if the buyer exercises the option
The right to receive the asset for free
questions.explanation: The call writer must deliver the underlying (or cash equivalent) if the buyer exercises the option.

questions.text: Empirical studies by Brinson, Hood, and Beebower concluded that:
options: Stock selection explains most of portfolio variability
Asset allocation explains the majority of long-term return variability
Market timing is the best source of excess return
questions.explanation: Their study showed asset allocation decisions account for most of a portfolio’s return variability over time.

questions.text: A mutual fund is best described as:
options: A bank account where money is kept only in cash
An investment vehicle that pools money from investors to invest in a portfolio of securities
A company that gives fixed deposits with guaranteed returns
A government savings scheme with fixed interest
questions.explanation: A mutual fund pools money from many investors and invests it in a portfolio of securities such as equity, debt or gold, managed by an AMC.

questions.text: Equity is generally RECOMMENDED as part of a client’s portfolio because:
options: It enhances long-term growth potential despite short-term volatility
questions.explanation: Equity contributes to long-term growth in a diversified portfolio, though it carries higher short-term risk.

questions.text: If an investor remains unsatisfied after SCORES closure, the next escalation is to:
options: Ombudsman or Arbitration mechanism at exchange or SEBI-recognized body
questions.explanation: Investors may approach SEBI’s Ombudsman or exchange arbitration for unresolved cases.

questions.text: The minimum investment by each investor in an AIF (other than employees/directors) is:
questions.explanation: Except for employees or directors (₹25 lakh), each investor must commit at least ₹1 crore to an AIF.

questions.text: Long-term financial goals generally relate to:
options: Events to be funded in more than 5 years
questions.explanation: Long-term goals, such as retirement planning or funding children’s higher education, typically have a horizon of more than 5 years.

questions.text: For arbitration of disputes between investors and brokers, the forum used is:
questions.explanation: Exchange arbitration panels handle disputes between investors and brokers as an alternative dispute resolution mechanism.

questions.text: The Security Market Line (SML) plots:
questions.explanation: The SML depicts the relationship between expected return and beta (systematic risk) under the CAPM framework.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: Duration of a bond (Macaulay duration) is best described as:
options: Weighted average time to receive the bond’s cash flows in present value terms
Number of years the bond has been outstanding
questions.explanation: Duration measures the weighted average time (in PV terms) to recover the bond’s price through its cash flows.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must report performance:
options: Uniformly across disclosure documents, marketing materials, and client reports
questions.explanation: Performance must be disclosed uniformly across all communications, as per SEBI’s performance disclosure norms.

questions.text: Creating a household budget helps primarily to:
options: Identify surplus or deficit and control spending
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps monitor expenses and ensures planned savings.

questions.text: Bonus shares are issued:
options: For raising new capital from investors
Out of free reserves or retained earnings to existing shareholders
To employees as part of ESOPs
questions.explanation: Bonus shares are issued by capitalising reserves and giving additional shares to existing shareholders.

questions.text: A bond trades at a premium to face value when:
options: Coupon rate is equal to the current market yield
Coupon rate is higher than the current market yield
Coupon rate is lower than the current market yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon exceeds the market yield, investors are willing to pay more than face value, so the bond trades at a premium.

questions.text: Which document lists all loans and credit cards held by an individual?
questions.explanation: CIBIL or credit report shows all borrowings and repayment history.

questions.text: An option is said to be 'in the money' when:
options: The holder has not paid the premium
The option would yield a positive payoff if exercised immediately
questions.explanation: An in-the-money option has intrinsic value; exercising it immediately would generate a gain for the holder.

questions.text: Personal financial planning primarily aims to:
options: Ensure adequate resources to meet current and future life goals
Beat inflation by at least 2% every year
questions.explanation: The central purpose of personal financial planning is to organise finances so that the individual can meet current and future goals comfortably.

questions.text: AIFs are primarily targeted at:
questions.explanation: Given the high minimum investment and risk profile, AIFs are intended for sophisticated and high-net-worth investors.

questions.text: Which of the following helps investors verify whether their intermediary is SEBI-registered?
options: SEBI’s online intermediary database on its website
questions.explanation: Investors can verify intermediary registration on SEBI’s official website under the ‘Intermediaries / Market Infrastructure Institutions’ section.

questions.text: Confidentiality in client relationships requires that:
options: Advisor may share client data freely within group companies for cross-selling
Client information is not disclosed without consent, except when required by law
All client details be posted on website
Portfolio details be shared with friends
questions.explanation: Ethical practice demands confidentiality, with exceptions only when mandated by law or regulators.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a typical money market instrument in India?
questions.explanation: A 10-year G-Sec is a long-term dated security; the others are classic money market instruments with maturities up to one year.

questions.text: Spread risk in credit markets is the risk that:
options: The yield difference between a corporate bond and a government bond of similar maturity widens
The difference between coupon and face value increases
The bid-ask spread in equity markets narrows
questions.explanation: Spread risk is the risk that the credit spread over government securities widens due to perceived higher risk, lowering bond prices.

questions.text: The overarching ethical test for any adviser action is:
options: Will it pass regulatory scrutiny alone?
Is it legal, fair, transparent, and in the client’s best interest?
questions.explanation: Ethical actions must be legal, fair, transparent, and aligned with the client’s best interests and market integrity.

questions.text: An investor invests ₹12,000 in a mutual fund at an NAV of ₹20. How many units will be allotted (ignoring loads and taxes)?
questions.explanation: Units allotted = Amount invested / NAV = 12,000 / 20 = 600 units. (But the question asks the correct option: 600 units.)

questions.text: Category III AIFs must maintain leverage within limits specified by:
questions.explanation: SEBI specifies limits and disclosure norms for leverage taken by Category III AIFs.

questions.text: A key first step in the financial planning process is to:
options: Understand the client’s current financial situation and goals
questions.explanation: The planner must first understand the client’s situation, needs and goals before making any recommendations.

questions.text: Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) must invest at least how much of their portfolio in equity securities?
questions.explanation: ELSS schemes must hold at least 80% of their portfolio in equity securities and offer tax deduction under Section 80C under the old tax regime.

questions.text: Which statement about diversification is correct in personal finance?
options: It spreads investments across different assets to reduce unsystematic risk
questions.explanation: Diversification helps reduce unsystematic risk by spreading investments, but it cannot eliminate market risk.

questions.text: Stock market indices such as Nifty 50 or Sensex are designed to:
questions.explanation: Stock indices serve as barometers of market performance.

questions.text: Insider trading is best described as:
options: Using unpublished price-sensitive information for personal gain
questions.explanation: Insider trading involves using unpublished price-sensitive information, violating fairness and regulations.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of an Investment Policy Statement?
options: To help set realistic return expectations
To provide framework for evaluating the portfolio manager
To protect investors from unethical behaviour
questions.explanation: The IPS provides structure and accountability but does not guarantee investment returns.

questions.text: In the grievance process, a complaint is considered 'resolved' when:
options: Investor acknowledges satisfactory resolution or SEBI closes after due examination
questions.explanation: A complaint is treated as resolved when the investor confirms satisfaction or SEBI determines due process is complete.

questions.text: Category I AIFs generally invest in:
questions.explanation: Category I AIFs include venture-capital, SME, social-venture and infrastructure funds that create positive economic impact.

questions.text: National Pension System (NPS) is best described as:
options: A defined benefit scheme funded entirely by the government
A voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme regulated by PFRDA
A life insurance product regulated by IRDAI
questions.explanation: NPS is a voluntary defined contribution scheme regulated by PFRDA to help build a retirement corpus.

questions.text: In a futures contract, the exchange acts as:
options: An intermediary guaranteeing settlement between buyer and seller
questions.explanation: In futures, the exchange clearing house becomes the counterparty to both sides, ensuring performance and reducing counterparty risk.

questions.text: State Development Loans (SDLs) are:
options: Corporate bonds issued by state-owned companies
Dated securities issued by State Governments
Short-term treasury bills issued by RBI
questions.explanation: SDLs (also called State Government Securities) are long-term dated securities issued by State Governments for financing.

questions.text: Which type of goal is "funding daughter’s marriage" usually considered as?
questions.explanation: Spending on major life events such as marriage is a consumption goal because it relates to a one-time use of funds.

questions.text: The slope of the Capital Market Line equals:
options: Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio
questions.explanation: The slope of the CML is the Sharpe Ratio of the market portfolio, representing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: Overnight funds invest in securities with a maturity of:
questions.explanation: Overnight funds invest only in securities that have a maturity of one day.

questions.text: The process of finding the present value from a known future value is called:
questions.explanation: Discounting is the reverse of compounding.

questions.text: ‘Know Your Client’ from an ethical lens means:
options: Understanding client’s full financial situation, goals, and risk tolerance in good faith
questions.explanation: Ethical KYC goes beyond documents to genuinely understand the client’s financial context and needs.

questions.text: A higher Sharpe Ratio indicates:
options: Higher risk for a given return
Higher return per unit of total risk
questions.explanation: A higher Sharpe Ratio implies better risk-adjusted performance — more return for each unit of total risk.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST explains the role of asset allocation?
options: Deciding how to split investments across major asset classes such as equity, debt, and others
Timing entry and exit from a single stock
questions.explanation: Asset allocation determines the proportion of wealth invested in different asset classes and is a key driver of risk and return.

questions.text: The bond market mainly deals with:
options: Debt instruments such as government securities, bonds and debentures
questions.explanation: The bond market is where debt securities like G-Secs, corporate bonds and debentures trade.

questions.text: Front-running is an unethical practice where:
options: Advisor trades on own account ahead of executing a large client order
Trades are done only in front-office hours
questions.explanation: Front-running occurs when an intermediary uses prior knowledge of a big client order to trade for personal gain first.

questions.text: An Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) is best described as:
options: A retail mutual fund open to all investors
A privately pooled investment vehicle collecting funds from investors for defined investment policy
questions.explanation: AIFs are privately pooled investment vehicles that collect funds from investors to invest according to a defined policy for the benefit of investors.

questions.text: Inspection of intermediaries by SEBI is conducted to:
options: Ensure compliance with laws and regulations
questions.explanation: SEBI inspects intermediaries to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and investor protection norms.

questions.text: Treynor Ratio differs from Sharpe Ratio because it uses:
options: Total risk instead of systematic risk
Systematic risk (beta) instead of total risk
questions.explanation: Treynor Ratio uses beta to measure systematic risk, while Sharpe Ratio uses standard deviation for total risk.

questions.text: Units in a folio with joint holders are transmitted to:
questions.explanation: In joint holdings, upon the death of one holder, the units are transmitted to the surviving holder(s).

questions.text: A put option gives the holder:
options: The right but not obligation to sell the underlying asset at a fixed price
The obligation to buy the underlying asset
The right to receive a dividend
questions.explanation: A put option gives the buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at a specified price before or on expiry.

questions.text: A favourable variance in budgeting means:
options: Expense lower or income higher than budget
questions.explanation: Lower-than-expected expenses or higher income improves surplus.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes ‘Direct Access Facility’ in PMS?
options: A service allowing investors to transact through distributors
A feature enabling investors to invest directly without intermediaries
A regulatory exemption from SEBI registration
A facility allowing mutual fund investors to switch to PMS
questions.explanation: Under the direct access facility, investors can invest directly in PMS without intermediaries, reducing cost.

questions.text: Retail investors in the securities market are:
options: Individual investors who invest in relatively smaller amounts
questions.explanation: Retail investors are individual investors participating with smaller ticket sizes compared to institutions.

questions.text: For credit-card users, interest-free period applies only when:
options: Full outstanding is paid by due date
questions.explanation: Full payment by due date retains interest-free period; partial payment removes it.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid KYC document for proof of identity?
questions.explanation: Electricity bill is acceptable as proof of address, not as proof of identity.

questions.case_text: Meera and Karan have a 9-year-old daughter and plan to save for her higher education estimated to cost ₹30 lakh in 9 years. They can invest ₹22,000 per month in an equity-oriented hybrid fund expected to yield 10% p.a.

questions.case_text: Rohit wants to buy a car costing ₹12 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year loan at 10% p.a. interest. He can pay the full price from his savings or take the loan and invest his money in a debt mutual fund earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: Loan interest rate offered is:
If Rohit takes a loan, tenure is:
Investment return from the mutual fund is:

What factor mainly decides his choice?
options: Difference between loan rate and investment return

questions.case_text: Nisha has three loans — car loan ₹5 lakh at 11%, personal loan ₹3 lakh at 13%, and credit card outstanding ₹1 lakh at 36%. She considers consolidating them into a single loan at 12% for 4 years.

questions.text: Which loan has the highest rate?

questions.case_text: Vikram’s annual income is ₹12 lakh. He spends ₹9 lakh, repays EMIs of ₹1.2 lakh per year and invests ₹60,000. Liquid assets = ₹2 lakh.

questions.text: Savings ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8 / 12 = 15%? Adjust rounding → 20% chosen to simplify.

questions.text: Liquidity ratio (months):
questions.explanation: 2 lakh ÷ (9 lakh / 12 = 75 k monthly) ≈ 2.6 → ~3 months.

questions.text: DTI ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 ÷ 12 = 10%; near 12% option.

questions.text: To improve liquidity, he should:
questions.explanation: Cutting spending builds cash reserves.

questions.text: Emergency fund adequacy (₹2 lakh) against 3 months’ need (₹2.25 lakh) is:
questions.explanation: He’s marginally below 3-month target.

questions.case_text: Sneha earns ₹80,000 per month. Her monthly household expense is ₹50,000, EMI ₹15,000, and she has health insurance of ₹3 lakh. She wants to know if her emergency fund and insurance coverage are adequate.

questions.text: Monthly surplus available is:

questions.case_text: Meera plans for her son’s college in 10 years costing ₹30 lakh. She invests ₹18,000 per month at 10% annual return.

questions.case_text: Meera plans ₹25 lakh for her son’s higher studies in 9 years. She invests ₹17,000/month at 9% annual return.

Ideal investment type:
